National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Details of Proceedings
17 Jestha 2083
Sunday
Meeting
Number - 19
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 12:17 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, the proceedings of today's National Assembly meeting will commence. (12:37 PM)
Honourable members, names of honourable members have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. I have allocated one minute each to every honourable member to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Urmila Aryal.
Honourable Mr. Urmila Aryal (Communist Party of Nepal): - Right Honourable Chairperson, (..voice not audible..) it is said to be mid-level expansion, and in the Madhesh region, the problem of drinking water has become severe again. In Madhesh, either the feudal class or extremely low-class people reside, so they have to drink water from pits, and sometimes they cannot bathe. If the water supplier digs up to 400 feet deep, they get slightly better water, but there is a severe problem with drinking water. I want to draw the government's attention that while the government may be focusing on other issues of mid-level development, it has not been serious about the issue of drinking water. Thank you. (12:38 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Uday Bahadur Bohora.
Honourable Mr. Uday Bahadur Bohora (Communist Party of Nepal): - Right Honourable Chairperson, the technical team of China Geological Company has submitted a report after collecting magnetoric and geochemical samples in Daldele, Dailekh district, and according to that report, there is a deposit of 1 billion 120 million cubic meters of methane gas, enough for Nepal for 50 years. Although the theoretical aspect of this project was mentioned in the government's budget speech for FY 2083/084, no budget has been secured to advance the excavation program. Therefore, I request the government, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, to commercially excavate this gas reserve and include this program within the FY 2083/084 programs. Thank you. (12:19 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina.
Honourable Mr. Goma Devi Timalsina (Communist Party of Nepal): - Right Honourable Chairperson, the budget for FY 2083/084 presented by the Honourable Finance Minister might have been prepared with great effort. However, it feels like a pickle without salt or sourness to us. We have heard many times outside that industries will be operated, but no allocation has been made in the budget. Therefore, industries do not run by mouth; they require practical implementation and budget. How will the government solve the problems of poor farmers, labourers, and landless people? I demand that this be informed to the House. Thank you. (12:20 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Durga Gurung.
Honourable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to the electricity-related problems faced by the citizens of Birendranagar, the capital of Karnali Province, and Surkhet. There has been a problem of low voltage in Birendranagar for a long time. Due to insufficient electricity supply, citizens are facing difficulties in their daily lives. Especially at night, they have to sit in darkness, which affects students, business people, and the general public. I request the Government of Nepal and the concerned bodies to take initiative. Thank you. Jai Nepal. (12:21 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
Honourable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Communist Party of Nepal): - Right Honourable Chairperson, the 132 KV transmission line from Surkhet to Kohalpur has been obstructed for two weeks due to a broken high-tension line caused by a storm. It is difficult to proceed with construction there as it falls within a protected area. I want to draw the government's immediate attention to this. Furthermore, Right Honourable Chairperson, we honourable members have spoken many times during Zero Hour and Special Time. However, there has been no response from any government minister to the demands we have raised. I want to draw the government's attention, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, to the demands raised by us honourable members during Special Time and Zero Hour, and I request the Right Honourable Chairperson to take initiative in this regard. Thank you. (12:22 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Narayan Datta Mishra.
Honourable Mr. Narayan Datta Mishra (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable Chairperson. (..microphone not audible..)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar.
Honourable Mr. Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal): - Right Honourable Chairperson, caste-based untouchability and discrimination are structural crimes. We apologize to the Dalit community, but Dipa Nepali, holding a banner saying 'Room Available,' has been protesting in the Mandala for a month. The government is not ready to provide justice. There are no programs to end discrimination in the budget speech of the 15th either. Just as the saying goes, 'No matter who the ascetic is, the ears are pierced,' I demand swift justice from the government. Thank you. (12:25 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable Chairperson, today the public is still suffering from the burden of inflation, and the silence of the head of government during the Republic Day celebrations has hurt both democracy and the republic. Observing some deluded, illusory golden deer jumping around in the name of constitutional amendment raises suspicion of a repeat of Sita's abduction. Right Honourable Chairperson, the menace of monkeys and bulldozers was already there. Now there is also a menace in the name of good governance and money laundering. Right Honourable Chairperson. All revolutions and movements in Nepal have been led by the middle class. What else can one call those who have now declared their intention to lead the middle class, leaving the poor and landless in the lurch, other than painted jackals? Finally, seeing that the report submitted by the Human Rights Commission to investigate the DNG movement has returned without holding high-ranking officials accountable, public trust has diminished. Thank you. (12:24 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, the turn for honourable members to speak during Zero Hour concludes here. Honourable members, I inform you that there will be no Special Time in today's meeting. Honourable members, the National Assembly meeting will be adjourned and reconvene after 20 minutes. (Thereafter, the meeting was adjourned to reconvene after 20 minutes.) Adjourned: 12:27 PM.
The National Assembly meeting, adjourned by notice today, commenced at 2:48 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, the proceedings of the National Assembly meeting will commence today. (2:48 PM)
Honourable members, in accordance with Rule 232 (d) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I have formed a Women's Coordination Committee in coordination with all the parties represented in the House, as stipulated in the rules, to build a common understanding on issues related to gender advocacy and to bring such understandings to the floor for debate. I propose the names of the honourable members to be included in that committee as follows:
1. Honourable Member Durga Gurung
2. Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary
3. Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhal
4. Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gере
5. Honourable Member Renu Chand
6. Honourable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota
7. Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota
Honourable members, I request you to give your consent to the proposal of honourable members for the Women's Coordination Committee.
Honourable members, I inform you that the proposal of honourable members for the thematic committee has received the consent of the House.
Honourable members, I inform you that the proposal of honourable members for the Women's Coordination Committee has received the consent of the House.
Honourable members, I now provide time to the Honourable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, to present a proposal received from the House of Representatives with a message from the Right Honourable Prime Minister and Home Minister, Balendra Shah, for discussion on Clause-by-Clause discussion on the "House of Representatives Member Election First Amendment Bill, 2083."
Honourable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam: - Right Honourable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present before the esteemed House the proposal to conduct clause-by-clause discussion on the "House of Representatives Member Election First Amendment Bill, 2083," received from the House of Representatives with a message. Thank you. (2:50 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, I now put the said proposal to a decision. Honourable members, those honourable members in favour of the proposal will say "Aye" and those honourable members against it will say "No."
Honourable members in favour of this proposal will say "Aye."
- "Aye"
Honourable members against this proposal will say "No."
As the sound of "No" was not heard, I declare that the proposal to conduct clause-by-clause discussion on the "House of Representatives Member Election First Amendment Bill, 2083," received from the House of Representatives with a message, has been unanimously approved.
Honourable members, clause-by-clause discussion on the "House of Representatives Member Election First Amendment Bill, 2083," received from the House of Representatives with a message, will commence.
Honourable members, I inform you that in accordance with Rule 106 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, three amendment proposals have been registered by 12 honourable members within the stipulated time for this bill. I will now provide time to the honourable members who have registered amendment proposals for the said bill to participate in the discussion with their respective amendment proposals, in order. First, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, I give time to Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar to participate in the discussion with his amendment proposal. Maximum time is five minutes.
Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal): - Right Honourable Chairperson, regarding the bill to amend the "House of Representatives Member Election Act, 2074," presented by the Honourable Minister, we had registered an amendment proposal from our group. We had proposed to add the following provision after Schedule 1. According to this, it states that when a political party nominates candidates according to this schedule, the representation of persons with disabilities must also be ensured. This is because this provision was not present in the bill that has come before this parliament. However, upon further study, I found that this matter is already present in Sub-rule 6 of Rule 28 of the main Act. It is a provision that the party must ensure the representation of persons with disabilities and those from backward regions. Therefore, the objective of our proposal, which we had presented to the parliament, did not seem significant. However, it is stated that arrangements should be made. We want to ensure this, and regardless of what happens, since this is present in it, this amendment of ours is being withdrawn.

I want to include. And in this context, what I want to state is whether it is appropriate or not. There is a community called Khassarya here. This might be a constitutional matter. What I want to state regarding this is, rather than possibly, from my personal perspective, the naming of a group or cluster as Khassarya, in relation to the 'Arya' part, Muslims are also 'Arya'. Madhesis are also 'Arya'. Dalits are also 'Arya'. But they have separate clusters. There is Dalit, there is Madhesi. So, in the naming of this Khassarya group, what is the rationale behind 'Arya'? What would have been the rationale for naming it? I want to state this. Although this matter is related to constitutional amendment. That's one thing. And regarding the quota, special facilities, and inclusivity, the term Khassarya is used here. Regarding this too, what I want to state is that such special arrangements, whether it's caste-based quotas, reservations, or proportional representation, or inclusivity, this is for backward communities, those who are marginalized by the state, or those who lack access to state power, deprived communities, and communities deprived of opportunities and rights. In the context of Nepal, is the entire Khassarya community such a community? Indigenous nationalities are. Dalits are. Madhesis are. Muslims are. Is the entire Khassarya community like that? There are individuals in the Khassarya community. They are poor economically. That is true. Not all people from the Khassarya community have become Prime Ministers, Ministers, Ambassadors, Secretaries, etc. But when talking about the entire community, giving special facilities like this might not be appropriate. If we do this, what will happen is, like the United Nations, or organizations like the United States, China, Japan, Germany, France seeking facilities, won't it be like that? I feel so. Therefore, therefore, the matter of constitutional amendment is also being discussed. I wanted to specifically point towards this issue. And finally, again, the amendment we have proposed to the 'Election to the House of Representatives Act, 2074' is an arrangement we have proposed for amendment in the Election to the House of Representatives Act itself. Therefore, I want to withdraw it. Thank you. I want to withdraw it on behalf of the group. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, from the proponents of the joint amendment motion (14:56), I give time to Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar to participate in the discussion with the proposal for amendment. Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson (14:56) Sir, we are in the clause-by-clause discussion of the bill to amend the Election to the House of Representatives Act, 2074. Honorable Chairperson, what we have proposed as our amendment to this bill is that an explanatory section be added to the schedule of this bill, and the phrase 'ensuring the representation of persons with disabilities' be added, according to this schedule. Similarly, in the table of the schedule, the word 'Terai Dalit' should be added after the word 'Dalit'. We have presented this proposal. Honorable Chairperson, for a very long time in Nepal, persons with disabilities have been a community that has been extremely marginalized socially, economically, and politically. More than approximately 2.2 percent of Nepal's population, more than 647,000 persons with disabilities reside in Nepal. But despite such a large number, their political participation is still very challenging. Article 42 of the Constitution of Nepal clearly states that participation in state bodies must be based on the principle of proportionality. Article 84 of the Constitution of Nepal also has provisions related to the proportional electoral system in the formation of the House of Representatives, and it is stipulated that the closed lists submitted by parties must include proportional representation. Similarly, Article 84(3) of the Constitution clearly directs that persons with disabilities must be included. Honorable Chairperson, on December 18, 2082, the Supreme Court issued an interim order in the name of the Election Commission, directing the political parties to include persons with disabilities in the closed list and also issued an interim directive. The Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, 2006, ensures the political participation of persons with disabilities. The Act Relating to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, 2074, also ensures the political participation of persons with disabilities. In this context, regarding persons with disabilities becoming members of the House of Representatives, their representation is still not legally ensured. Section 28(6) of the Election to the House of Representatives Act states that representation of persons with disabilities should be ensured when nominating candidates, but subsection (6) of Section 60 of the same Act does not make it mandatory, due to which persons with disabilities are unable to be elected as members of the House of Representatives. In 2079, persons with disabilities did not get to represent parliament through various political parties. However, in the 2082 elections, due to the interim order of the Supreme Court and the interim order of the Election Commission, it appears that all parties have ensured the representation of persons with disabilities. In this context, while this Act is being amended, if provisions can be clearly made in this Act to ensure the representation of persons with disabilities, then in the future, the political representation of persons with disabilities in the House of Representatives can be ensured. In this context, since the Honorable Minister is also present here, while bringing this Act forward, how will it ensure the representation of persons with disabilities in the future? What is the government thinking? I would like to know the government's stance on that. And finally, I would also like to state that the representation of Terai Dalits within the Dalit community is extremely low. It can even be said to be non-existent. Therefore, efforts should be made to amend this Act to ensure the representation of the Terai Dalit community. I will express my views after hearing the government's stance. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, from the proponents of the joint amendment motion (14:01), I give time to Honorable Member Khamm Bahadur Khati to participate in the discussion with the proposal for amendment. Time limit is five minutes. Honorable Mr. Khamm Bahadur Khati (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, I wish to request an amendment to Schedule 1 of the Election to the House of Representatives Act, 2074, which is currently in effect. Firstly, concerning Schedule 1, Section 28, subsection 5 is included, which is based on the principle of inclusivity. And in subsection 6 of this section, there is an important point where it is stated that backward regions and persons with disabilities must be included. And Article 84(2) of our constitution mentions backward regions, and Article 84(3) also protects the rights of persons with disabilities, which is guaranteed by the constitution and the law. However, in this schedule, Section 28, subsection 5 is included, but subsection 6 is not. This means that Section 28(6) should have been included in this schedule, but it has not been included. And subsection 6 of Section 60 is mentioned as being related to this. It is not compulsory. Because it is not compulsory, to secure the right to ensure or the fundamental rights granted by the constitution, the existing provisions in the Act and the census based on them have resulted in six clusters being placed here. And backward regions and persons with disabilities are not included in them. I think this might have been an oversight when creating these clusters. Because the same provision is in the regulations. There are six clusters, which include Dalit, Indigenous Nationalities, Khassarya, Madhesi, Tharu, and Muslim. Backward regions and persons with disabilities are not included. Therefore, my first request is that we have regulations to regulate this. Regulation 14(1) has provisions for persons with disabilities and backward regions in both clusters. This does not mean that what is guaranteed by the Act and the constitution is not included in the current schedule. Therefore, my request is that it be included. Along with this, while we are discussing here, we have proposed amendments to Section 106. There will be no inconvenience in adding or modifying. And in case of conflict with the constitution, the Act becomes void. And considering the content of the regulations, it is in practice. Persons with disabilities are also given representation, and backward regions are also given representation. But based on the census, there might have been a lack of homework. Therefore, it should be included immediately. This will bring harmony between the constitution, the Act, the law, and the regulations. And I have stated these points. Honorable members and ministers are also present here. And I humbly request them that we are not just speaking for the sake of speaking. When we talk about the constitution, laws, or Acts, and about the rights of the marginalized, it is more appropriate to include them. And this is also about the fundamental rights of individuals. Therefore, I request the Honorable Minister that we are not trying to create controversy for the sake of controversy. This proposal has been made after a thorough discussion and consideration for resolution and to protect the rights of the people. We have no objection if this bill is passed with this amendment. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, now the House of Representatives has sent the message regarding the 'Election to the House of Representatives First Amendment Bill, 2083'. I request the honorable members who wish to participate in the clause-by-clause discussion on the amendment proposal to submit their names within two minutes. I have allocated three minutes to each honorable member participating in the discussion. Honorable Member Dharmendra Paswan. Honorable Mr. Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, my amendment proposal is that after the word 'Dalit' in Schedule 1 of the Election to the House of Representatives Act, 2074, the word 'Terai Dalit' should be included. Honorable Chairperson, out of the total 13.8 percent Dalits in Nepal, Madhesi Dalits constitute 4.9 percent, but the representation of Madhesi Dalits has always been low, sometimes zero. In the 2082 elections, the representation of Madhesi Terai Dalits in the parliament is zero. Honorable Chairperson, currently, Terai Dalits constitute 4.9 percent of the population in Nepal, but in the House of Representatives, the Dalit Commission, other

The presence of Tarai Dalits in commissions, Public Service Commission, police, and army has been zero or minimal at times. The constitution clearly states that there should be representation based on the population of Madhesi, Tharu, Muslim, Janajati, and all other minority ethnic groups. From time to time, the Election Commission has misinterpreted this, resulting in zero representation for Tarai Dalits. This is why Dalit movements have occurred in Nepal from time to time, and they have not been successful. This is because Tarai Dalits were not present. Madhesi Dalits could not participate. However, Tarai Dalits in the Madhesh region have been seen to agitate from time to time. But the Nepal government has not listened. If this amendment is not made, there is a possibility of a major incident in the Madhesh region. It is seen that movements have already started in the last two-three days regarding the landless and the budget. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel.
(15:08 hrs)
Honorable Shri Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML):-
(15:08 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson Sir, thank you for the time.
We are discussing the bill to amend the House of Representatives Election Act. The main subject of discussion is the manipulation of the schedule. What is the source for manipulating this schedule? The source is Section 28, Sub-section 5 of the House of Representatives Election Act. What does this sub-section 5 say? It states that when a party prepares a closed list of candidates in accordance with this section, it must prepare it according to the inclusive principle, ensuring representation of Dalits, Janajatis, Khas Arya, Madhesi, Tharu, and Muslims, among others, based on geographical and regional balance, as mentioned in Schedule 1, considering population. The Act provides that only the percentage of representation for each community will be written in the schedule. Therefore, we have not discussed amending this section. We have discussed the matters in the schedule as per this section. Therefore, I believe we need to discuss the number of community clusters, which are the six specified clusters. Therefore, I don't think there is much to discuss here. However, what we need to pay attention to is that the population of the Dalit community has decreased from 13.8 to 13.4. Now, in some municipalities and metropolitan cities, including Kathmandu, some communities within the Newar community are elected from the Dalit community cluster, identifying themselves as Dalit. However, they are not listed as Dalit in the schedule. They are in the list based on population. They are counted in the numbers. But they are benefiting from the facilities for Dalits based on population. When becoming a candidate for the House of Representatives, people from that community are represented. They become candidates. But they are not counted in the cluster they belong to. Where is their population counted? Their population is counted under Indigenous Nationalities, not Dalits. Therefore, such matters need to be reconciled. We must stop the practice of population being counted in one place and benefits being taken from another. This is my first request. Secondly, as raised earlier, the representation of the Madhesi Dalit community in the House of Representatives was zero this time. Therefore, in such matters, which section needs to be amended? The government should pay attention to which section needs to be amended. The representation of the Madhesi community in the House of Representatives must be ensured, the representation of the Madhesi Dalit community. If they are pushed into the Madhesi quota, and if Dalits are pushed into the Dalit quota, where will the Madhesi Dalits go? Therefore, to ensure this, attention must be paid to amending other sections of the Act. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, received from the House of Representatives with a message.
(15:12 hrs)
The discussion on the clause-by-clause deliberation of the "Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, 2083" will conclude here. Honorable members, now I will provide time to the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, to respond to the questions raised during the discussion.
Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs Shri Sovita Gautam:-
(14:92 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson Sir, in today's "Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, 2074", honorable members had also submitted amendments, and now they have presented their views during the discussion. The issues raised by you are very sensitive given the sensitivity of the subject matter. These are issues that need to be incorporated appropriately. However, technically, we have held discussions with the amendment-proposing honorable members in formal and informal settings. There are various points that have arisen. We are positive about the government addressing them. However, I must state here that the representation in the proportional electoral system is based on the 2078 census report. Schedule 1 was amended by the previous government before the 2082 House of Representatives election, through an ordinance, and this replacement bill has been brought to replace it. Now, since it is based on the census data, it is a bit difficult for us to discuss those data points here. And the issue of including Tarai Dalits, as you have raised, is a very valid point. Similarly, the representation of backward regions and persons with disabilities must also be ensured. Their representation must come to the parliament ensured. This is also a very appropriate issue. Now, what I can tell you is that the original Act, Section 28, Sub-section 6, and the original Act, Section 60, Sub-section 6, mention the provision for representation of backward regions and persons with disabilities. Since it is written in the original section, we have had extensive discussions on whether to write it in the schedule or not. It is currently in practice. However, the phrase "as far as possible" is used in Section 60, Sub-section 6. In the replacement bill, Section 60 was not touched, only the schedule was modified. Therefore, I would like to urge you that the Bill to Amend and Consolidate Election Laws is currently under consideration. When it comes to parliament in the future, the government is committed to inclusively incorporating all the issues you have raised. I express this commitment on behalf of the government. Although the government is ready to address all the issues raised here in principle, it seems somewhat difficult to incorporate them at this point from a drafting perspective. Therefore, when our Bill to Amend and Consolidate Election Laws comes, we are committed to discussing your issues extensively and incorporating them with a very open heart. This is what I want to express on behalf of the government, and the honorable members have submitted amendments. We have understood your sentiments. I also urge you to withdraw your submitted amendments. That's all I have to say, Honorable Chairperson, thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, received from the House of Representatives with a message.
(15:96 hrs)
The clause-by-clause deliberation on the "Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, 2083" concludes here. Honorable members, now the amendment proposals received from the House of Representatives regarding the "Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, 2083" will be presented for decision sequentially. Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, I give time to Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar to withdraw his amendment proposal if he wishes to withdraw it.
Honorable Shri Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party):- (..mic inaudible) I had already stated my views. However, the Honorable Minister has just made a commitment. These issues of persons with disabilities and backward regions are indeed very sensitive. Therefore, we had said that this issue must be included for that reason. It is also in the Act. Moreover, since the Minister has already made a commitment, we do not see much justification for our amendment. Therefore, on behalf of the entire group, I would like to inform you that we have withdrawn our amendment proposal. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar has withdrawn the amendment proposal submitted by him regarding various sections and sub-sections of the "Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, 2083" received from the House of Representatives, so the proposal does not need to be presented for decision. Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, I give time to Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar to withdraw his amendment proposal if he wishes to withdraw it.
(15:18 hrs)
Honorable Shri Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson Sir, while discussing the amendment proposal we submitted, the Honorable Law Minister of the Government of Nepal stated that it can be addressed in the context of the upcoming Bill to Amend and Consolidate Election Laws, and also spoke about representation in many sections, clauses, and sub-sections of the current House of Representatives Election Act. Considering the assurance given by the Honorable Minister, and with the belief that the participation of persons with disabilities in policy-making will be ensured through future laws, I would like to inform you that I am withdrawing the amendment submitted by our group.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar has withdrawn the amendment proposal submitted by him regarding various sections and sub-sections of the "Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, 2083" received from the House of Representatives, so the proposal does not need to be presented for decision.
Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, I give time to Honorable Member Khamm Bahadur Khatri to withdraw his amendment proposal if he wishes to withdraw it.
Honorable Shri Khamm Bahadur Khatri (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson Sir,
(15:20 hrs)
I had previously and boldly expressed my views on this matter. And our Law Minister has clearly stated that the House of Representatives Election Act,

In Section 5 of the 2074 Act, it is based on the principle of inclusivity, and Section 6 refers to the context of the marginalized and disabled. The constitution guides this, and the regulations have also come into practice. Regarding commitment to this, or in the context of the House of Representatives Election Act, due to the positive thinking you have expressed, and in accordance with Article 110 of the National Assembly Regulations, the proposal I had put forth, and which we had put forth and discussed. In the context of this proposal, it has been accepted that it is not aligned in the near future, and what needs to be considered is that out of the six clusters, two clusters remain to be added, which is constitutional and legal, and the current regulations have a purely existing provision. The technical aspect is that it has reached 100% in these six clusters. It cannot be otherwise. However, keeping in mind how much is for the disabled and how much is for the marginalized, and with the commitment to amend in the upcoming act, I request to withdraw my amendment proposal. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, Honorable Member Kham Bahadur Khatri has withdrawn the amendment proposal presented by him regarding various sections and sub-sections of the "House of Representatives Election First Amendment Bill, 2083", which was received with a message from the House of Representatives. Therefore, the proposal does not need to be presented for decision.
Honorable members, now I present for decision whether Sections 2 and 3 of the bill, the "House of Representatives Election First Amendment Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, should be passed. Honorable members in favor of this proposal will say "Yes" and honorable members against it will say "No".
Honorable members in favor of this proposal, say "Yes".
- "Yes"
Honorable members against this proposal, say "No".
No "No" voices were heard. Therefore, I declare that Sections 2 and 3 of the bill, the "House of Representatives Election First Amendment Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, have been passed unanimously.

Short Title and Commencement: 1. This Act shall be called the House of Representatives Election First Amendment Act, 2083. 2. This Act shall come into force immediately.

Honorable members in favor of this proposal will say "Yes" and honorable members against it will say "No".
Honorable members in favor of this proposal, say "Yes".

Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson, the government has presented the "Voter List Act, 2073" Amendment Bill, which is to amend the "Voter List Act, 2073", with the message from the House of Representatives. We are discussing it. As far as this bill is concerned, our group's attention has been drawn to the addition in Section 2. Five honorable members from our group had submitted amendments. It states to add sub-section 2(a), and it says that notwithstanding anything written in sub-section 2, in the event that the House of Representatives is dissolved before the completion of its term and an election date is announced, the Election Commission may set a period for the collection and registration of voter lists and their updating for the purpose of such an election. Regarding this, our group's opinion is that, firstly, it says "notwithstanding anything written in sub-section 2" in sub-section 2(a). Sub-section 2 was about regular elections. There were legal provisions made to address that. Does this phrase prohibit that sub-section? I would like to know the government's opinion on this. And secondly, it says "the Election Commission may set a period" before the completion of the House of Representatives' term, which leaves it to the discretion of the Commission. Such matters should not be left to the discretion of the Commission. It must be bound by law. Our group felt that a law should be made, and we submitted this amendment. Our amendment is that after the word "Commission", it should be stipulated that the collection and registration of voter lists and their updating must be completed one month before the nomination filing date for candidates. We want to know the government's opinion on this. The government's opinion on this has not yet been formally clarified. Therefore, we want to know this opinion, and then we will state what we will do from our group's side.
Along with that, I would also like to mention something else: Honorable Chairperson, this is a law made for a specific task created in specific circumstances. It is not a law made for any program after the end of the House of Representatives in the regular manner for regular elections. And therefore, we felt that a law must be made for such a situation. Moreover, this is an emergency event, but it has happened in the past. It happened very recently. I see a high probability of it happening again in the future. Because in a country like Nepal, the House of Representatives and the National Assembly are not dissolved. To dissolve them, the entire system must be dissolved. The constitution itself must be abolished. And the demand was not made by the Janji movement on the 23rd and the criminal incidents on the 24th. Therefore, this National Assembly remains appointed. It cannot be said in the context of the House of Representatives. Therefore, it can happen again and again. For this reason, a law must be made. And thus, all these things, collection of voter lists, registration, updating, must be done. The Election Commission does it. And it does it by setting a specific period. Therefore, rather than leaving it to the Election Commission, the law should stipulate it, is what we want to say. And even if regular elections are held, in such a situation where the term ends prematurely due to dissolution, the Election Commission does give some time for voter list registration. When that is done, it happened in the past, it is happening now, and there is a possibility of it happening in the future, so why not make a law? A law must be made. Why is an ordinance needed? is what we felt. And similarly, at this time, rather than considering where the ruling party and the opposition are, who was where, who is where, this is a matter of law, a matter of procedure, a matter of policy, therefore we saw the need for such a provision and have introduced this amendment. But again, in the end, Honorable Chairperson, what is the government's clear opinion on this? Our proposal is that voter list collection and registration should be done one month before the nomination of candidates. What is the government's opinion on this? After knowing this, we will state whether we will withdraw or do something else. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, on behalf of the joint amendment proposers, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, with the amendment proposal, for discussion...

I will give time to participate, time is 5 minutes.
Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson
(14:34 hrs)
Regarding the Bill to Amend the 'Voter List Act, 2073'
Sir,
We are participating in the clause-by-clause discussion. And
Respected Chairperson, elections are an extremely indispensable aspect of any democratic country. It is a tool. It is an important event through which elected representatives gain legitimacy and reach the process of governing the state.
However, while discussing elections, we need to consider three specific aspects. We all talk about elections being free, fair, and credible, highlighting the three theoretical aspects of elections. Specifically, whether an election is fair or not is determined by when and how the voters participating in the election are selected.
21
Now, in that context, regarding the provisions that have come up for registering names in the voter list, especially the provision 2(a) that allows registration of names in the voter list after the election has been announced. If we talk theoretically, it is not theoretically correct to register names in the voter list after the election date has been announced. Our current laws also do not consider it correct. However, the issue that has come up in this bill is that in a situation where the House of Representatives has been dissolved and an election has also been announced, in a country like Nepal with a specific demographic structure, all communities, all age groups may not be able to register their names in the voter list in time. Since only a smaller population will participate in voting if names are not registered in the voter list, considering that, the government has brought the provision of 2(a). Theoretically, some agreement can be reached on that. However, we cannot agree with the government's proposal to allow the Election Commission to collect voter lists by setting a deadline at any time, as the government has proposed. Specifically, we cannot agree with the open-ended provision proposed in 2(a) that allows voter registration even after the date for nomination of candidates has been announced.
Therefore, on behalf of our group, we have proposed that the program to register names in the voter list should be completed before the date of nomination. The Honorable Minister of the Government of Nepal is here. What is the government's stance on this? Let it come formally. After hearing that, we can think about it with some flexibility. I have presented these points on behalf of our group. Thank you.
Respected Chairperson: Honorable members, on behalf of the proponents of the joint amendment proposal,
(15:38 hrs)
I give time to Honorable Member Roshri Meche to participate in the discussion with the amendment proposal, time is 5 minutes.
Honorable Mr. Roshri Meche (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Respected Chairperson
(15:38 hrs)
Sir, we are in the process of clause-by-clause discussion on the 'Voter List Act, 2073' First Amendment Bill recently presented by the Government of Nepal. Now, what is the provision brought by the government is that by adding sub-clause 2(a), they have proposed that notwithstanding anything written in sub-clause 2, in a situation where the term of the House of Representatives is about to expire, the House of Representatives is dissolved and the election date is announced, the commission may set a period for the collection, registration, and updating of the voter list for the purpose of such an election. We have jointly submitted an amendment proposal to this. Now, our joint opinion on this is that by adding this (a), what will happen is that the collection and updating of the voter list is a regular process of the Election Commission, it is a continuous program, so the Election Commission has to do this work. It is happening continuously. For example, it is happening continuously every year at the end of Chaitra. Therefore, I want to request this.
Also, if we bring this provision and the election is announced, what will this provision do regarding the collection of voter lists? It can raise a question regarding the fairness and transparency of the election, which are our principles. Therefore, I want to request that this provision raises doubt about whether it will make the election fair or not.
Another thing is that after the election date is announced, all political parties are focused on the election. And will their attention be on the collection of voter lists, or will all stakeholders be focused on it? Also, an administrative complexity will arise. All the administration will be involved in the election. Since all administrative staff will be engaged in how to make the election effective, transparent, and inclusive, I see an administrative complexity arising.
Chairperson Sir, the collection of voter lists cannot be linked only to elections. This is a regular duty of the state. Therefore, the state has to perform this work regularly. I want to ask why this voter list collection needs to be done under special circumstances.
Another thing is that this ordinance has come as a replacement bill, and we see that bringing this ordinance before the election to collect the voter list also weakens the legal stability. Therefore, this provision that has come should be removed.
23
Furthermore, to strengthen the credibility, transparency, and legal stability of the election process, we jointly believe that it is appropriate to remove the proposed amendment to sub-clause 2(a) of clause 4 from this bill. And another thing I want to mention here is that the voter list collected by bringing this ordinance after the election was announced, our party should have spoken at that time in special circumstances, it was wrong to collect the voter list by bringing this ordinance. At that time, our country was in a state of turmoil. Historical structures were burning, and due to that, we did not oppose the work of collecting the voter list by bringing the ordinance, and we remained silent thinking that it should be continued. But what is in the current provision in the 'Voter List Act, 2073', keeping it as it is, and removing this proposed provision, is my opinion. Thank you.

Chairperson Sir, this replacement bill on the ordinance regarding the 'Voter List First Amendment Bill, 2073' has come. If we read this Voter List Act from beginning to end, it is a prohibitive act. It states who are voters, who are not, what constitutes an offense, who votes, and who does not. It is a kind of prohibitive law. It doesn't say who is not. It specifies who is. And in the context of specifying this, when do such voters exist? And who are these voters? This act talks about voters for the House of Representatives. It talks about the National Assembly, the President and Vice-President elections, and it talks about the standards for voters in provincial and local levels. And it focuses on what is not.
Therefore, as our honorable amendment proposer mentioned earlier, regarding the incident of August 23 and 24, due to the mid-term election during that time, there was a demand to update the voter list as an extra task for the Election Commission, even though it is a regular task. To address that demand, the then government brought an ordinance, adding 2(a) to clause 4 of the 2073 Act. What this did was allow the Election Commission to update some voter lists by extending the deadline. This allowed the prohibitive act. And bringing this replacement bill was not necessary. In fact, this was supposed to be repealed. And it is in a situation where the old rules and acts related to voter registration, which were thought out and done better, should have been kept alive.
Therefore, the Election Commission's work is done throughout the year. When the election is announced, after the announcement, you are prohibited from doing it. It is stopped. It is prohibitive. It is your regular work throughout the year. You can do it anytime. But when the election date is announced, you are told not to do it. The reason behind saying so is to prevent the danger of manipulation of voters, transparency, accountability, and fairness in elections. Recently, in India, in the election held in West Bengal, there have been many disputes regarding the voter list, and this is an issue that we have been resolving for a long time. To say that it can be done anytime is wrong, it should not be said, and our request is that this bill should be withdrawn by the government. Thank you.

Honorable Mr. Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Thank you
(15:47 hrs)
Respected Chairperson. Respected Chairperson, our constitution's provision and our practice do not envision the dissolution of the House of Representatives. Because, as we all know, the Supreme Court has overturned the dissolution of the House of Representatives twice, and the recent provision is that if the government cannot be formed under any circumstances, the Prime Minister will be appointed under Article 76(4), and such a Prime Minister will not even need a party whip to take a vote of confidence, so the House of Representatives will give a Prime Minister in any case. No. Otherwise, this replacement bill should be withdrawn by the government, that is the first request. Now, if we do this tomorrow, what will happen is that as soon as mid-term elections are held, by-elections are also a type of mid-term election. Therefore, as soon as elections are announced in every place, voter registration should be collected within a specified time. People from the neighboring village, taking the law with them, one candidate would make them voters in another place, and then after winning the election, after the election is over, they would move back to their original place. This kind of distortion can occur. This will prevent elections from being fair, impartial, and free from rigging. Therefore, this provision should be kept, this is the second point. The third point is that players cannot be added after the game has started according to the rules of the game. Once the election is announced, the players are decided, aren't they? sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting commenced at 12:17 PM under the chairmanship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The Chairperson announced the start of the proceedings and the allocation of time for Zero Hour.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening of the meeting and Zero Hour procedures

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: Several members raised issues during Zero Hour. Urmila Aryal highlighted the drinking water crisis in Madhesh. Uday Bahadur Bohora discussed the potential of methane gas in Dailekh and urged for its excavation. Goma Devi Timalsina expressed dissatisfaction with the budget's lack of support for industries and solutions for the poor. Durga Gurung pointed out electricity problems in Surkhet. Nar Bahadur Bisht raised concerns about the Surkhet-Kohalpur transmission line and the lack of government response to previous concerns. Narayan Datta Mishra and Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar spoke about caste discrimination and the need for justice. Yuvraj Sharma criticized inflation, government silence, and the potential for constitutional amendments to be misused, also mentioning the DNG movement report.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel initiated a discussion on the Bill to Amend the House of Representatives Election Act, focusing on the manipulation of the schedule and the representation of various communities, particularly Dalits. He highlighted discrepancies in population data and benefit allocation. The Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, responded, acknowledging the sensitivity of the issues and the government's commitment to addressing them in future legislation, particularly regarding the representation of Tarai Dalits, backward regions, and persons with disabilities. She requested the withdrawal of submitted amendments.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar presented an amendment proposal regarding the "Voter List Act, 2073" Amendment Bill. He raised concerns about the discretion given to the Election Commission and proposed a specific timeframe for voter list updates.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Padam Bahadur Pariyar of the Nepali Congress spoke about the 'Voter List Act, 2073' Amendment Bill. He argued that while theoretically correct, allowing voter registration after an election announcement is problematic. He suggested that registration should be completed before the nomination date. Honorable Roshri Meche of the Nepal Communist Party (UML) also discussed the bill, expressing concerns about administrative complexities and the potential impact on election fairness. He proposed removing the provision allowing voter registration after an election announcement.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Ram Kumari Jhankri of the Nepal Communist Party (UML) analyzed the Voter List Act, describing it as a prohibitive law. She argued that the ordinance allowing voter registration after an election announcement was unnecessary and that the existing laws should be maintained to ensure election fairness and prevent manipulation. Honorable Somnath Poudel of the Nepal Communist Party (UML) discussed the constitutional provisions regarding the dissolution of the House of Representatives and the possibility of mid-term elections, referencing past events and the current government's potential actions.
